brief: Oil and AI capex are hitting the same Treasury-buyer pool at once. Houthi strikes shut the Saudi East-West pipeline, Saudi output sits at a 30-year low near 6m b/d, and the WTI/10-year correlation has hit 0.96, so every barrel higher adds basis points to the long end. Hyperscaler capex above 100% of operating cash flow implies $1.3tn of debt by 2028, and tech leads $380bn of 2026 bond supply, competing directly with Treasuries. Historically hiking cycles push the 10-year up more than 100bp. Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid says brace for 6% before the Fed is done. Goldman says the S&P typically falls 2% in a tightening cycle's first three months, then gains 9% over the next 12, 2022 excepted. Nomura's McElligott calls the energy shortage the macro regime driver, with bonds, equities, gold, credit and crypto weakening while the dollar, energy equities, commodity carry, rates trend and long volatility are the hiding places. But Deutsche Bank's bond-positioning gauge sits near the 5th percentile, the most-short end of its range, so the hike is priced but the reaction is not. CTAs already short duration could be forced to cover if yields reverse lower, the short-squeeze risk the title names.
